newsitem.title: SPAIN: Worried NATO backs Bosnian Serb leader Plavsic.
newsitem.headline: Worried NATO backs Bosnian Serb leader Plavsic.

text.p: NATO leaders expressed support on Tuesday for Bosnian Serb leader Biljana Plavsic in her battle with Bosnian hardliners and voiced deep concern over "the increasingly anti-democratic climate" in the country.

"The democratic process is being distorted in order to block the constitutional decisions of the elected president of Republika Srpska which must be respected," they said in a statement issued at a NATO enlargement summit in Madrid.

The statement called on hardliners supporting indicted war criminal and ex-Bosnian Serb president Radovan Karadzic to resolve their differences peacefully, warning they faced even greater isolation from the international community if not.
"We will not tolerate any recourse to force or violence, or the unauthorised deployment of military or paramilitary force," the statement said.

NATO countries lead a 35,000-strong peace force, policing the peace accords which brought an end to more than three years of bitter conflict in the country where tens of thousands of people were killed.
But they have been criticised for failing to take action to detain Karadzic whose influence remains immense and who has fallen out with one-time ally Plavsic in a row over illegal smuggling rackets.
